text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPaleontologyNew Feathered Dinosaur is the First Megaraptor Discovered in EuropeIts name means “unconquered female warrior”JCBy Jake Currie5:00 PM CDT on October 14, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleEngland may have a reputation for bleak weather, but the Isle of Wight is closer to dreamy than dreary. The small, diamond-shaped island off the southern coast has sun-drenched beaches and microclimates warm enough for tropical plants. Of course, 120 million years ago, it was even toastier, featuring a lush sub-tropical landscape populated by dinosaurs. Now paleontologists have discovered a new Cretaceous creature that lived there, and it’s proving to be an important piece in the puzzle of megaraptor migration.  Powered By 10 ShareNextStayA team of paleontologists identified the new species from a partial braincase unearthed from the Isle of Wight in 1924 by an amateur paleontologist. The specimen was discovered after a century spent languishing in a drawer of England’s Natural History Museum. Once brought to light, the team performed micro-CT scans to create 3D models of the interior and exterior of the skull. Read more: “This Newly Discovered Dinosaur Looks Terrifying—But Probably Wouldn’t Eat You”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
